newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn declines comment on Eurostat Italy decision.
newsitem.headline: Bonn declines comment on Eurostat Italy decision.

text.p: The German Finance Ministry said on Friday it had no comment on the European Union's decision to allow Italy's eurotax as part of its efforts to qualify for European monetary union.
Previously, the Italian plan for a special tax to reduce its deficit had appeared to meet with German disapproval of "creative bookkeeping".
A Finance Ministry spokeswoman, commenting on Friday's decision by Eurostat, the EU's statistical arm, told Reuters, "It is up to Eurostat to decide. We would not care to comment."
Eurostat said the Italian tax is in accord with the uniform accounting rules of the European Union.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel had in past months warned prospective EMU particpants against "creative bookkeeping" in their efforts to meet the EMU criteria.
Italian premier Romano Prodi said during a visit to Bonn in February that Italy was not engaging in creative bookkeeping, nor could it afford to do so.
